Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team ran the SIG questionnaire and flagged an item around ephemeral session logs. Specifically, for a subset of our integration tests we need a 90-day window of session-level logs tied to tenant IDs for a limited pilot so our internal auditors can run traceability checks.

Per Redwood's default policy we understand session logs are normally retained for 30 days and then truncated. Pharmacor is asking whether Redwood can agree to a timeboxed exception for 90 days for the pilot tenant pharm-pilot-01. We'll need evidence artifacts (sample export, retention policy statement, and a signed attestation) to include in our internal audit packet.

I've attached the SIG section and a small CSV sample of the session rows we'd expect. Can you let us know if this is possible and what controls you would apply (access, encryption, deletion confirmation) during and after the extended retention window?

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear ask and the samples. We're open to supporting a timeboxed exception for an identified pilot tenant but need to confirm a few operational and compliance guardrails. High level: we can retain session-level logs for up to 90 days for a scoped tenant with the following controls by default:

- Limited access list (RBAC) for the audit artifact: only Pharmacor owners + Redwood compliance (read-only)
- Server-side encryption with customer-specific KMS key (if requested for Private customers) or Redwood-managed CMEK for Hosted/Dedicated
- Audit trail of who accessed the logs and automated deletion runbook at T+90 + 24-hour manual verification window
- Export formats: CSV or encrypted archive with checksum and signed manifest

Before we proceed we'll need:
1) written agreement on the scope (tenant name, timeframe)
2) a signed minimal addendum to the existing contract (we can provide a template)
3) confirmation of whether Pharmacor needs Redwood to use a customer-provided KMS (Private) or if Redwood CMEK is acceptable (Hosted/Dedicated)

I'm looping in Evelyn (Legal/Compliance) and Karthik (Solutions) to validate operational feasibility and sign-off. Can you confirm the tenant identifier and whether Pharmacor will be using a dedicated KMS?

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Customer Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi all — after internal review Redwood can approve a 90-day retention exception scoped to tenant pharm-pilot-01 with the following binding controls and deliverables:

1) Scope & timing: 90 calendar days starting 2027-06-15 through 2027-09-13.
2) Access controls: RBAC whitelist (Pharmacor auditors + Redwood Compliance). Any access generates immutable audit entries stored for 1 year.
3) Encryption: Redwood CMEK will be used for the pilot.
4) Evidence deliverables: monthly access attestation (PDF), final deletion certificate with checksums and backup wipe confirmation, and an exported encrypted archive (on request) before deletion.
5) Contract addendum: Redwood will provide a scoped addendum (two paragraphs) that documents the exception and deliverables; Pharmacor signs prior to start.
6) Cost: there will be a nominal one-time operational fee covering the guarded storage and manual verification steps (we'll include a quote in the addendum).

Next steps Mina: prepare the addendum and the operational runbook (who will have RBAC, how to request exports, escalation path). Karthik, please prepare the runbook and a sample deletion certificate template.

Thanks — Evelyn Hart
Head of Compliance, Redwood Inference
